ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Pablo Neruda — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three-month review: PSA and testosterone, thyroid function, blood count and chemistry, glucose, radiotherapy effects, the rash, the second leuprolide injection, and plans for the year

text.paragraph: Three-month review on androgen deprivation with apalutamide, after radiotherapy to the prostate. [S]

Mr. Neruda returns three months after starting treatment, with a professional Spanish interpreter. He finished 20 fractions of radiotherapy to the prostate three weeks ago. During the last two weeks of treatment he had more frequent urination and looser stools, and both are settling: he now gets up once a night, and his bowels are once or twice a day, with no bleeding. The rash he had five weeks ago faded within two weeks on the cream and cetirizine, and he has stopped both. The hip pain has gone; he has not taken acetaminophen for three weeks. Hot flashes come four or five times a day. His weight is up 2 kg, and he tires in the afternoons but still walks daily and writes every morning. He has had no falls. His home blood pressure readings have been around 130/80 since the amlodipine increase. He asks whether the treatment is working. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1971-09-14; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Regular rhythm; blood pressure 132/80 mm Hg; no ankle swelling
No rash; mild darkening of the skin over the radiotherapy field

Urinary frequency, weak stream and nocturia for four months, with right hip and low back pain for six weeks, a hard nodular prostate and a raised PSA; suspected prostate cancer, to be confirmed
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when biopsy and staging established metastatic prostate cancer.

Adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Grade Group 4 (Gleason 4+4), cT3a N1 M1b, de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, low volume by conventional imaging (two bone metastases, in the right ilium and L5, and two pelvic lymph nodes; no visceral disease); synthetic modern detail linked to his documented prostate cancer of 1916
S — Synthetic grade, stage, extent and PSA; the prostate cancer and the operation in France in 1971 are documented (D), and no stage, grade or treatment detail was found in the sources read.

Pelvic lymph node metastases: right external iliac and right obturator nodes

list.item:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, three months on treatment (C61). Good response: PSA 0.18 ng/mL, at or below 0.2 ng/mL, which predicts a better outcome; testosterone 14 ng/dL; alkaline phosphatase back to normal at 96 U/L. Somatic testing of the biopsy found no alteration in the homologous recombination repair genes, and the tumor is microsatellite stable. [S]
Second leuprolide 22.5 mg injection today.
Continue apalutamide 240 mg daily.
PSA and testosterone every three months; imaging if PSA rises or new symptoms appear.

After radiotherapy to the prostate (Z92.3). Grade 1 urinary and bowel effects, settling. IPSS 9, down from 17 before treatment. [S]
Report blood in the urine or stool at any time.

Raised TSH on apalutamide (R94.6). TSH 5.4 mIU/L with free T4 1.0 ng/dL: subclinical, without symptoms of hypothyroidism. Raised TSH is common on apalutamide. [S]
Repeat TSH and free T4 with the lipid panel in about eight weeks; levothyroxine if free T4 falls or TSH rises above 10.

Androgen deprivation with apalutamide (Z79.899). Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, mildly low, as expected; hemoglobin A1c 6.1 percent, up from 5.9; weight up 2 kg; hot flashes four or five times a day. [S]
Walking and resistance exercise; fewer sweets at official dinners.
Lipids and the statin decision at the annual wellness visit in three weeks.

Bone metastases (C79.51). Pain resolved. [S]
Acetaminophen stopped.

Apalutamide rash (L27.0). Resolved without stopping apalutamide. [S]
No treatment needed.
